topic.seo_intro:
TP53, commonly known as the "guardian of the genome," is a tumor suppressor gene that plays a critical role in protecting cells from becoming cancerous. When functioning normally, the TP53 gene produces a protein that stops the growth of abnormal cells and triggers their destruction if they become damaged. However, TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in human cancers, found in approximately 50% of all cancer cases across multiple types including breast, colorectal, lung, and ovarian cancers. Understanding TP53 mutations has become essential for cancer researchers and clinicians seeking to develop better diagnostic tools and targeted treatment strategies.

The study of TP53 as a biomarker has revolutionized how researchers approach cancer diagnostics and prognosis. TP53 mutations can serve as important indicators of cancer risk, disease progression, and potential treatment response. By analyzing TP53 status in tumors, oncologists can better understand the biological characteristics of a patient's cancer and make more informed decisions about therapy options. This genetic information has opened new pathways for personalized medicine approaches in cancer care, allowing for more precise and individualized treatment plans based on each patient's unique tumor profile.

On this page, you'll find comprehensive information about TP53 in cancer research, including its role as a diagnostic biomarker, recent clinical findings, and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting TP53-mutated cancers. The articles and research summaries below represent the latest peer-reviewed studies from leading cancer research institutions, providing evidence-based insights into how TP53 research is advancing our understanding and treatment of cancer.

articles.title: Transient p53/p21 activation selectively protects healthy human hair follicles and their stem cells from chemotherapy.
articles.hook: ALRN-6924 protects hair follicles from chemotherapy damage via p53/p21 activation
articles.summary: A drug called ALRN-6924 protects healthy hair follicles and stem cells from chemotherapy damage by temporarily halting their growth.

articles.title: Hitting pause on chemotherapy-induced alopecia: transient p53 activation as a guardian of the hair follicle.
articles.hook: p53 activation protects hair follicles from chemotherapy damage
articles.summary: A drug that activates p53 protects hair follicles from chemotherapy damage, potentially preventing chemotherapy-induced hair loss.

articles.title: A potential mutation-defined POLE/MMR/TP53 group classifications to stratify BRCA wild type epithelial ovarian cancer.
articles.hook: POLE/MMR/TP53 mutations stratify outcomes in BRCA wild-type ovarian cancer
articles.summary: Researchers propose new genetic classification system to better predict outcomes in ovarian cancer patients without BRCA mutations.

articles.title: Serositis as possible manifestation in MDS/AML patients with complex karyotype and TP53 mutation: case series.
articles.hook: TP53 mutations linked to serositis manifestation in MDS/AML patients
articles.summary: Patients with blood cancer carrying p53 mutations developed inflammation treated successfully with steroids.

articles.title: Activating p53Y220C with a mutant-specific small molecule.
articles.hook: TRAP-1 reactivates mutant p53Y220C in cancer cells, inducing death
articles.summary: Scientists developed a drug called TRAP-1 that reactivates mutant p53 in cancer cells, triggering cell death and senescence.

articles.title: Eprenetapopt in combination with Palbociclib exerts synthetic lethality in mantle cell lymphoma.
articles.hook: Eprenetapopt and Palbociclib combination kills mantle cell lymphoma cells
articles.summary: Combining eprenetapopt and palbociclib shows promise against mantle cell lymphoma by targeting mutant p53 and cell cycle control.

articles.title: Resveratrol coordinates apoptosis and autophagy in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via p53 acetylation: An integrative network pharmacology and experimental validation study.
articles.hook: Resveratrol triggers dual cell death pathways in hepatocellular carcinoma via p53 acetylation
articles.summary: Resveratrol kills liver cancer cells by activating a protein called p53, which simultaneously triggers two death mechanisms: apoptosis and autophagy.

articles.title: Trp53 loss drives the neoplastic transformation of Pik3caH1047R-induced vascular malformation in a mouse model.
articles.hook: P53 loss transforms PIK3CA-mutant vascular malformations into angiosarcoma**
articles.summary: PIK3CA mutation causes vascular malformations in mice, while additional p53 loss promotes rare transformation to angiosarcoma.

articles.title: Oncogenic MAGEA4 directs neuroendocrine differentiation and survival in prostate cancer cells through the SIRT1/Acetyl-p53/BCL-2 axis.
articles.hook: MAGEA4 protein drives neuroendocrine prostate cancer via SIRT1/p53/BCL-2 pathway
articles.summary: Researchers found that MAGEA4 protein drives aggressive neuroendocrine prostate cancer growth and resistance through a specific molecular pathway.

articles.title: Native Mass Spectrometry Reveals Binding Modes of the Tumor Suppressor Protein p53 to Different DNA Response Elements.
articles.hook: Native mass spectrometry maps p53 binding to full DNA response elements
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that p53 tumor suppressor protein requires its complete 20-base DNA binding site and tetrameric structure to form stable, functional complexes with DNA.
